title: Cyclotomic action on signed point-line section coordinates
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ with $q=p^a$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($n\ge1$) [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Set $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $g=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ with $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$. Choose primitive roots $\zeta_r\in k$ of order $\ell^r$ with $\zeta_{r+1}^{\ell}=\zeta_r$ and put $e=(\zeta_r)_r$. For $B=\mathcal O_E$ or $A_{E,n}$ use the signed sheaf twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], the sheaf Weil isomorphisms $\tau_m^B:g^{-1}B(m)_s\to B(m)_s$ [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists], and the restriction/coprojection maps $\sigma$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. Put
$$\Psi_m^B=\Gamma(s,\tau_m^B)\circ\sigma_{B(m)_s}:\Gamma(s,B(m)_s)\to\Gamma(s,B(m)_s).$$
The corresponding root-level composite sends $\zeta\in\mu_{\ell^r}(k)$ to $\gamma(\zeta)=\zeta^{q'_r}$, where $q q'_r\equiv1\pmod{\ell^r}$. Its inverse-image comparison [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image] at $(s,g)$ is the identity on the roots of the unchanged underlying scheme. These maps commute with $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^{\ell}$, and their limit sends $e$ to $q^{-1}e$. Write $e_B=e\otimes1$, $e_{m,B}=e_B^{\otimes m}$ for $m>0$, $e_{0,B}=1$, and $e_{-r,B}(e_{r,B})=1$ for $r>0$. The coefficient factors of $\Psi_1^B$ fix $1$. For all $b\in B$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$,
$$\Psi_m^B(b e_{m,B})=b q^{-m}e_{m,B}.$$
More precisely $\Psi_0^B(1)=1$, $\Psi_{m+1}^B(e_{m,B}\otimes e_B)=\Psi_m^B(e_{m,B})\otimes\Psi_1^B(e_B)$ for $m\ge1$, and the induced dual action for $r>0$ is $\varphi\mapsto\varphi\circ(\Psi_r^B)^{-1}$, with $\Psi_{-r}^B(e_{-r,B})(e_{r,B})=q^r$. Here $q$ is a unit in $\mathbf Z_\ell$, and its image in $B$ defines the displayed signed powers.

proof.text: Compute the finite root action using the adjunction defining the root comparison, its direct-image projection formula and the pullback projection equation for the specified sectionArrow. Naturality of GammaSpecIso then identifies this action with geometric field Frobenius. Apply the roots-of-unity Frobenius power theorem to obtain the modular inverse exponent and the p-adic unit q.

The roots inverse-image isomorphism theorem gives the identity comparison in the normalized chart. Naturality of the inverse-image adjunction unit, transition compatibility of the root comparisons and naturality of the transition map show that the finite root actions commute with all displayed transitions.
Apply the completed-root-action lemma to the given section e. Each coefficient action fixes 1 simply because its three factors are ring homomorphisms.

Use the signed-section-scalar lemma on every section. It gives the formula on b times x by associativity and commutativity of scalar multiplication, and the degree-zero assertion because the scalar is 1. Bilinearity of the actual sheaf tensor gives the successor formula by inverse(q)^(n+1) times inverse(q) = inverse(q)^(n+2).

The p-adic unit q maps to a unit in the valuation ring, each finite quotient and each lifted scalar ring. Its positive and inverse powers cancel. The signed scalar formula and bilinearity of internal-Hom evaluation therefore give invariance of the pairing. Multiplication by q^(n+1) is an explicit two-sided inverse of the positive action, hence that action is bijective. Substitute invFun of the positive action into the pairing identity to derive the inverse-dual identity. Finally evaluate the negative scalar formula on the normalized generator; its value 1 leaves scalarAt(q^(n+1)).
